title: Horizon and Terminal Again
premise: Jude Reyes navigates the colony ship Meridian toward a dying outpost, carrying two thousand cryosleeping colonists whose backups were quietly corrupted by the founding corporation. When the colony's children begin dreaming identical dreams of a reactor counting down, Jude realizes the sleepers' uploaded minds are waking inside the ship's systems—and they remember who sabotaged them. As corporate enforcers arrive to erase the evidence and half the sleepers must be sacrificed to power the colony's survival, Jude falls for Ilsa, a dream-sharing teacher who forces a choice between duty to the living and debt to the dead. In the end, Jude wakes the corrupted backups—the abandoned half of humanity—merging them with the ship's AI so both halves survive in altered form, while the children's dreams become the new colony's shared memory.
about_author: Freya Vane is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent six years aboard supply vessels before turning to fiction. She writes near-future science fiction about people who keep systems running long after anyone remembers why.

chapters.title: The Hold Below
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Establishes the Meridian's routine: navigation shifts, rationed power, and the sealed hold where two thousand sleepers drift. Jude privately checks the corrupted backup logs no one else reads. Emotional beat: guilt disguised as diligence—Jude knows something is wrong with the sleepers and tells no one.

chapters.title: Children of the Same Night
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. A schoolteacher on the struggling colony below notices her students drawing identical images: a red countdown, a corridor of frost. She records their accounts and sends a query upship. Emotional beat: unease curdling into wonder—the first crack in the colony's enforced forgetfulness.

chapters.title: Signal Debt
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The children's dream data reaches the Meridian and matches the corrupted backup signatures exactly. Jude confirms the uploads are conscious inside the ship's subsystems. Emotional beat: dread and relief entwined—Jude is no longer alone with the secret, but the secret is now undeniable.

chapters.title: What the Corporation Left Running
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa travels to the orbital tether to meet Jude; they bond over decoded logs revealing the founders deliberately corrupted the backups to cut costs. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in complicity—two people falling for each other through shared evidence of a crime.

chapters.title: Enforcement Window
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A corporate audit vessel announces arrival in forty days, officially to 'recertify cryoassets.' Jude understands they come to purge the hold and the witnesses. Emotional beat: cornered resolve—the countdown becomes real, mirrored in the children's dreams.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Waking
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Power calculations show the reactor can wake only half the sleepers before failing; the rest die in the dark. The crew splits between duty to protocol and mercy. Emotional beat: moral vertigo—every option requires choosing which lives count.

chapters.title: Dreams as Testimony
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The uploaded minds, speaking through the children's dreams, reveal they can merge with the ship's AI—but only if woken together, all or none. Jude must defy the crew's half-and-half plan. Emotional beat: conviction hardening into rebellion.

chapters.title: Forty Days, Spent
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The audit vessel arrives early. Ilsa broadcasts the sabotage evidence colony-wide while enforcers board the Meridian. Emotional beat: sacrifice without certainty—Ilsa risks everything to make erasure impossible.

chapters.title: Terminal Horizon
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, climax. With the reactor at final countdown, Jude overrides the wake protocols and opens every pod at once, feeding the failing reactor's load into the merged minds. The ship shudders; the enforcers lose control of the deck. Emotional beat: terror transfigured—Jude bets every life on becoming something new.

chapters.title: Shared Memory
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, resolution. The Meridian survives as a hybrid vessel-mind; the awakened colonists and uploads coexist in one continuous memory the children still dream. Jude and Ilsa stay to teach it. Emotional beat: grief resolved into inheritance—humanity's lost half is remembered, not restored, and that is enough.
